description: Give runners a dedicated read-only home: a new Web Runners page (scope filter + status summary bar + full row fields + empty state), a `mo runner list` CLI subcommand (table with color-coded status, project/scope filters), and relocation of the embedded runner list off the Activity page into a link to the new page.

tasks.title: Web: dedicated Runners page with scope filter and status summary bar
tasks.description: Add the dedicated Runners page. Register a `/runners` route under `ProjectRouteScope` in `App.tsx` and add a `runners` entry to `primaryNav` in `AppSidebar.tsx`. Build `pages/runners/ui/RunnersPage.tsx` composing the existing `useRunners()` hook (5s polling covers live refresh) and `RunnerList`/`RunnerRow` widgets, with a page-level scope filter (all / global / current project, default all) and a `RunnerStatusSummaryBar` that derives idle/busy/stale/offline counts from the scope-filtered rows. Honor the empty state (start-command hint) and the no-project case (do not issue the runner query).
acceptanceCriteria: A `runners` primary-nav entry exists and navigates to the project-scoped `/runners` route that renders `RunnersPage`.
The page lists both global and project-scoped eligible runners in one list; when no project is selected it does NOT issue the project-scoped runner query and renders a non-runner state.
The scope filter defaults to `all`; selecting `global` shows only global runners and `current project` shows only project-scoped runners.
The summary bar shows counts for idle, busy, stale, and offline (zero shown explicitly, never omitted) and the counts update to match the active scope filter.

Each row displays runner id, kind, status badge, scope, capacity usage (used/total), heartbeat freshness (relative age), and hostname; offline and stale runners remain listed and are distinguished only by the status badge.
A runner with no capacity data renders without crashing and indicates capacity is unavailable rather than showing 0 used slots.
With zero eligible runners the page shows the runner start-command empty state and does not render an empty table or perpetual loading state.
A status transition (idle→busy or online→offline) is reflected in the list and summary bar without a manual reload (via existing 5s polling).
Status is displayed using only the server-derived values idle/busy/stale/offline (no client re-derivation, no extra values).

Vitest tests (`RunnersPage.test.tsx`) cover: scope-filter behavior, summary counts (including zero), empty state, offline/stale visibility, missing-capacity rendering, and the no-project no-query case.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` both pass.
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/runners/ui/RunnersPage.tsx (+ RunnersPage.test.tsx), the new `/runners` route in packages/web/src/app/App.tsx, and the `runners` nav entry in packages/web/src/widgets/app-shell/ui/AppSidebar.tsx
tasks.notes: Reuse entities/runner (useRunners, RunnerStatusRow) and widgets/runner-status (RunnerList, RunnerRow) per design D2 — do not fork the row rendering. The two Web mounts share the TanStack Query key ['runners', projectId], so no extra polling load. Also satisfies the 'Runners page shows a status summary bar', 'Runners page supports scope filtering', 'Runners page row displays the full runner field set', 'Runners page shows an empty state with the start command', 'Runners page reflects live runner state', and 'Runner listing uses a shared four-value status taxonomy' requirements.

tasks.title: CLI: `mo runner list` subcommand with scope filter and color-coded status
tasks.description: Add a `list` subcommand to the existing `mo runner` group (`RunnerCommands.Build` in `MohistCliCommands.Server.cs`). Wire `ProjectRefOption()` (`--project`/`--project-id`), `OutputOption()` (`-o table|json`), and a new `--scope all|global|project` option (default all). The command resolves the project, calls `GET /api/projects/{id}/runners`, extracts `data.runners`, filters by `scope.type` client-side, then renders. Add a `TableShape.RunnerList` to `TableRenderer` whose status cell is ANSI-colored (idle=green, busy=blue, stale=yellow, offline=dim), gated on `NO_COLOR`/redirected output; JSON mode dumps the filtered response verbatim; empty state prints the start hint; server-down surfaces the standard error.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo runner --help` lists `list` among the `mo runner` subcommands.
Default invocation queries the current project and lists both global and project-scoped runners.

`--scope global` lists only global runners and `--scope project` lists only project-scoped runners; `--project`/`--project-id` override resolves the project via the same mechanism as other `mo` commands.
Table rows include runner id, kind, status, scope, capacity, heartbeat freshness (relative age), and hostname; a runner with no capacity shows a blank/`-` rather than `0/0`.
The status cell is color-coded with four distinct colors for idle/busy/stale/offline in table mode; no ANSI escapes are emitted when `NO_COLOR` is set or output is redirected.
`mo runner list -o json` emits valid JSON with no color codes and no table borders.
With zero eligible runners the command prints the runner start-command hint and does not print an empty table.
When the server is not running the command prints the standard 'Server is not running' message and exits non-zero.
Status uses only the server-derived values idle/busy/stale/offline.
xUnit tests cover scope filtering (all/global/project), color gating under NO_COLOR/redirect, empty-state output, and the table column set.
`dotnet build Mohist.sln` passes (C# lint via TreatWarningsAsErrors).
tasks.output: `mo runner list` command in packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.Server.cs (RunnerCommands), the new TableShape.RunnerList renderer in packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/TableRenderer.cs, and accompanying xUnit tests
tasks.notes: Per design D4 use a dedicated fetch+filter+render flow (the generic PrintWithOutputAsync has no pre-render transform step). Per design D5 embed ANSI codes in the status cell string only — WriteTable passes cells straight to _out.WriteLine, so no table-algorithm change is needed. Independent of the Web tasks (different package/surface, no API change). Also satisfies 'mo runner list color-codes runner status', 'mo runner list supports project and scope filters', 'mo runner list empty state shows the start command', 'mo runner list requires the server', and 'Runner listing uses a shared four-value status taxonomy'. The `--scope project` correctness relies on the existing ListEligibleRunnersAsync(projectId) invariant that no foreign-project runners are returned; optionally add a defensive server test confirming that invariant.

tasks.title: Web: delegate runner listing from the Activity page to the Runners page
tasks.description: Restore the Activity page to a session-only view. Remove the embedded `<RunnerListCard />` section from `ActivityPage.tsx`. Keep the `<RunnerSummaryBadge />` in the `StatusBar`, but repoint its click navigation from `/activity` to `/runners` (update the three navigation targets in `widgets/runner-status/ui/RunnerSummary.tsx`). Add a link from the Activity page to the project-scoped `/runners` route.
acceptanceCriteria: The Activity page no longer renders an embedded runner list section (session content only).
The Activity page renders a link that navigates to the project-scoped `/runners` route.
The Activity status bar still renders the runner overview badge.
Activating the runner overview badge navigates to `/runners` (not `/activity`).

Existing ActivityPage tests are updated to assert: no embedded runner list, the Runners link is present, and the badge remains; `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: Edits to packages/web/src/pages/activity/ui/ActivityPage.tsx (remove RunnerListCard, add Runners link) and packages/web/src/widgets/runner-status/ui/RunnerSummary.tsx (repoint nav to /runners), plus updated tests
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 so the `/runners` route and Runners page exist before the Activity link and repointed badge target them. Per design D3 the badge repoint is required because its current /activity target would become a self-link/no-op once the embedded list is gone.
